headline: Warren Buffett hands Berkshire's chair to his son
summary: Buffett, 96, gave up the chairman title Friday in a letter to shareholders, nine months after handing the CEO job to Greg Abel. His son Howard, a director since 1993, takes the chair and will guard the firm's "culture and values." Buffett stays on the board as chairman emeritus. He took over Berkshire in 1965. It is now worth $1.1 trillion.

cover_question.q: Why is he giving his job to his son?

cover_answer: He's 96. He says the timing is right. His son takes over.
table_question: When is the right time to hand something you built to someone else?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Warren Buffett is 96 years old and was the boss of a giant company for 61 years. It owns Dairy Queen and part of Coca-Cola. Now he is giving the top job to his son Howard. It's like being team captain for a very long time and then handing the armband to someone else. He's still there to help.
5-7.why: A very old man handing his job to his kid is a story about families, which five-year-olds already understand.

8-12.script: Buffett took over Berkshire, a failing textile mill, in 1965. He bought solid companies and held them, and it is now worth $1.1 trillion. This year he gave the CEO job to Greg Abel, and Friday the chair to his son. A relay runner passing the baton before slowing down.
8-12.why: Planning your own replacement is a chain they can follow.

13-17.script: Would you trust a 96-year-old to pick who runs a $1.1 trillion company? Buffett picked Greg Abel to run it and his son to guard its "culture and values," worth more, he says, than any asset. Berkshire has lagged the S&P 500 for most of a decade. Late, or exactly right?
13-17.why: Teens like judging a legend, and the lagging numbers give them a lever.

5-7.q: Why is he giving his job to his son?
5-7.a: He's 96 and says it's time. His son has helped run the company for 33 years, and his new job is to keep it working the way his dad built it.

8-12.q: Is his son the boss now?
8-12.a: No. Greg Abel runs the company. Howard leads the board and guards its culture. Buffett calls him insurance you hope never to use.

8-12.q: How did he get so rich?
8-12.a: He bought solid companies at fair prices and held them for decades. Berkshire owns GEICO, Dairy Queen and a railroad.

13-17.q: Is Berkshire still any good without him?
13-17.a: Its stock is up 1% this year versus about 12% for the S&P 500, and it has lagged the index for most of a decade.

13-17.q: Why his son and not a professional?
13-17.a: Buffett says Greg runs the company and Howard guards its culture. Howard has been on the board since 1993.
